notes: Q2 FY26 (reported 2026-07-22) was a clean beat-and-raise: subscription revenue +24.5% YoY, AI ACV crossed $1B (agentic deployments up 9x in nine months), renewal rate held at 98%, cRPO +21% YoY, FY26 subscription guide raised to $15.76-15.78B. Stock initially sold off to $95.46 same day ('sell the news' on an already-battered name) then rallied to $115.76 by 2026-07-29, settling $111.23 — a genuine relief rally, not a fade, the first one of this derate cycle. This build sits at the tail end of an 18-month 'AI eats SaaS seats' selloff: NOW fell from an intraday/monthly ATH of $234.08 (2025-01-28, also a beat-and-raise day) to a trough of $83.00 (2026-04-10), a -64.5% drawdown, before a choppy, twice-tested recovery. The multiple compression is real (own-history NTM P/E fell from an elevated 2023-2024 regime toward today's ~25x) and the peer group shows a wide split: CRM/WDAY have derated further (13-14x) while SNOW still trades rich (139x) despite weaker margins — NOW sits in between, cheaper than its own recent history but not the cheapest name in the group. The crux open question, per CLAUDE.md's pull-forward-test analog: is AI ACV genuinely incremental (a new monetization layer on top of the existing workflow franchise) or is it relabeling/cannibalizing seat-based ARR that would have grown anyway? Q2's cRPO growth (21%, not decelerating) argues against pure cannibalization, but this is exactly the number to watch each quarter — see the bear case kill-switch.
